what: Strata SQ-15 on a TRUE single T4 (device-restricted), with drafting enabled
hardware: 2x Tesla T4 but restricted to gpu0 via --gpu 0 and CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0

vram_after_load_mib.note: gpu1 at 0 confirms the restriction held; this is a real single-card result

findings: Drafting IS active on a single T4: 331 draft tokens, 128 accepted, 38.7% acceptance.

The 2xT4 run had drafting OFF (0.98x probe) while this single-card run has it ON. The difference is that the earlier run's auto-probe measured a loss while this one cleared the engine's 1.10x bar, so the drafting decision is configuration-sensitive, not a fixed property of sm75.
Single T4: 22.6 tok/s with drafting, vs 18.3 tok/s on 2xT4 auto-split without it. One card with drafting beats two cards without.

Per-token cost is FLAT in N (24-31 ms from N=2 to N=32). That is the memory-bound signature: verifying a block of draft tokens costs about the same per token as one. So the batched-dequant hypothesis has empirical support from Strata's own engine.
correction_to_prior_claim: The earlier note said spec decode is a 0.98x loss on sm75 and that the path to 60 tok/s must be bytes moved alone. That was based on a 2xT4 run whose auto-probe disabled drafting. A single-card run enables it and accepts 38.7% of drafts. Spec decode is viable on T4; the earlier negative was a configuration artifact, not a hardware limit.
gap: 22.6 measured against 60 target: 2.65x to close, on one card, with drafting already on.
